title: Halal money scenarios
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 7 (Halal money scenarios (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: Lending, borrowing and riba. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Borrowing and lending
points: Borrow: take now, pay back later
Lend: give now, get back later

bullets: Banks and credit cards charge it

blocks.h: Money problems: choose a halal option

questions.q: Amir wants a £300 laptop for his studies. He has £120. A shop offers a credit plan that charges interest. What is a halal option?
questions.a: Save the £180 he still needs (for example £30 a month for 6 months), buy a cheaper or second-hand laptop, or ask family for an interest-free loan (qard hasan) and pay back exactly what he borrowed. The credit plan charges interest, which is riba.

questions.q: Yasmin's friend asks to borrow £10 and says, 'I'll pay you back £12 next week.' What should Yasmin do?
questions.a: Lend £10 and accept only £10 back. A fixed extra amount on a loan is riba. She can lend as a kindness, or say no politely if she cannot afford it.

questions.q: A family wants to keep their savings safe and growing. Choose a halal option and explain.
questions.a: A savings account with no interest, or an Islamic profit-sharing account based on real trade; avoid fixed-interest savings.

keywords.def: take money you must pay back
give money that will be paid back
extra money charged on a loan
interest on loans, forbidden in Islam (رِبَا)
a goodly loan with no interest (قَرْض حَسَن)

questions.q: Borrow £50 at 20% for one year. Paid back?

questions.a: A loan with no interest, given as a kindness.

questions.q: Core: Scenarios sheet: for three money problems, choose a halal option and explain (pupil PDF).
questions.a: Save first; borrow from family as qard hasan; buy second-hand.

questions.q: Extend: Explain in the portal response box why riba can harm people. Start: 'Riba can harm people because...'
questions.a: Riba can harm people because debts grow, the poor pay more and wealth flows to lenders.

questions.q: Borrow £200 at 10% for a year. Paid back?
questions.a: B) £220. 10% of £200 is £20, so £220. In Islam, this extra is riba.

questions.q: Riba is... A) charity B) interest on loans, forbidden in Islam C) a type of savings
questions.a: B) interest on loans, forbidden in Islam
options: Interest on loans, forbidden in Islam

questions.q: Big question: lend £10, ask £12 back: is it fair in Islam?
